item.title: Smoke and dye testing for San Antonio on Jan. 8
item.description: (Commonwealth Utilities Corporation) — Dye tests and smoke tests will be conducted in San Antonio, Beach Road on Thursday, Jan. 8, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The purpose of these tests is to identify leaks, breaks, and other connections in CUC’s sewer system. The post Smoke and dye testing for San Antonio on Jan. 8 appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Mayor RB restores Garapan basketball court’s backboard
item.description: (Press Release) — The Saipan Mayor’s Office, under the leadership of Mayor Ramon “RB” Camacho, continues its commitment to empowering youth through islandwide sports initiatives, despite ongoing challenges posed by vandalism and rising crime. item.title: Apatang meets with Federation of State Medical Boards
item.description: (Office of the Governor) — Gov. David M. Apatang met with representatives of the Federation of State Medical Boards or FSMB to discuss strengthened collaboration in healthcare regulation, physician licensure, and patient safety initiatives impacting the Commonwealth and U.S. jurisdictions nationwide. item.title: CNMI Medicaid launches provider directory, says it’s a ‘smarter way to connect with care’
item.description: (CMA) — The Commonwealth Medicaid Agency proudly announces the launch of its enhanced CMA Provider Directory, an innovative online resource designed to improve access to healthcare services and empower Medicaid beneficiaries throughout the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. item.title: Meth case sentencing postponed
item.description: THE sentencing of two defendants in a federal methamphetamine case has been postponed to Feb. 11 at 2 p.m., after Chief Judge Ramona V. Manglona granted the U.S. government’s request to continue the hearing previously set for Jan. 16. The post Meth case sentencing postponed appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Saipan mayor turns to businesses, nonprofits for road repair support
item.description: SAIPAN Mayor Ramon “RB” Camacho is calling on the business community, government agencies, quarry operators, and nonprofit organizations to help repair deteriorating secondary roads connecting Kagman to Laulau Bay, a popular tourist diving area. item.title: New law aims to encourage business development on Saipan
item.description: GOVERNOR David M. Apatang last week approved House Local Bill 24-34, establishing the Saipan Economic Incentive District. The post New law aims to encourage business development on Saipan appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Yeom disputes Post casino report
item.description: THE former executive director of the now-disbanded Commonwealth Casino Commission has pushed back against a recent Washington Post investigative article on the Saipan casino, saying claims about money laundering are based on speculation rather than evidence. The post Yeom disputes Post casino report appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.description: DIVING instructor William Saron Capayas is expected to plead guilty to possessing child pornography, according to a court filing. The post Diving instructor to plead guilty to child pornography charge appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Hopwood school construction may be rebid
item.description: THE Public School System may have to rebid the construction phase of Admiral Herbert G. Hopwood Middle School if the contractor, CJ Innovation, fails to meet the deadline to complete the architectural and engineering design of the new campus. The deadline is Jan. 31, 2026. The post Hopwood school construction may be rebid appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.
